subject: Volume commit optics + sprint credits — renewal negotiation
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Pierce <jpierce@orchid.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft renewal: smoothing commit curve + sprint credits idea

Jordan —

Thanks again for the candid convo last week. Per our discussion I put together a short set of options that aim to: 1) preserve unit economics for Orchid while 2) give you predictable committed capacity over the next 12 months as you ramp the new search workload.

Topline idea: convert a single-year commit into a phased volume-commit with a smoothing clause (quarterly ramp) + a small pool of "sprint credits" (one-time token credits) to help cover burst testing and go-live spikes. The sprint pool can be used within the first 90 days and then expires.

I attached a high-level pricing sketch (PDF) with three tiers: conservative ramp, standard ramp, and aggressive ramp. For transparency I kept the effective per-token price at each tier aligned with the Dedicated pricing ranges we reviewed.

Next step: are you open to sharing a target annual committed spend (range) so I can map the tiers to numbers that make sense for Orchid? If procurement wants a redlineable doc, I can also send a short amendment + SOW.

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(dylan_brooks@redwood.com)

Attachment: Orchid_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

From: Jordan Pierce <jpierce@orchid.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchid.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft renewal: smoothing commit curve + sprint credits idea

Dylan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. The sprint credits idea is helpful for our infra team's go-live tests. Procurement asked for a single consolidated number for forecasting, but they also want the option to front-load capacity if we hit early success.

Rough target: $650k-$900k committed spend over 12 months, but we expect the first quarter to be light and quarter 3 to be heavy. Can you show a variant that keeps our annual commitment in that band while allowing a 20% front-load option in Q3?

Also, procurement will need a clause limiting overage rates and a clear conversion rate for sprint credits to committed tokens.

Jordan
Head of Engineering | Orchid Labs
(jpierce@orchid.ai)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Orchid target and procurement asks — draft response

Dylan / Markus —

Jordan sent the ballpark numbers and procurement asks. Notes for the proposal:
- Keep three ramps but map the middle one to $750k ARR equivalent to sit inside their range.
- Add an explicit 20% temporary front-load (Q3) that triggers a short-term burst pool at a slightly higher per-token rate (we can give a 10% discount off standard overage to soften it).
- Define sprint credits as a one-time pool convertible at a 1:1 token equivalence; attach a short SOW that limits usage window to 90 days.
- Add an SLA credit schedule for latency-sensitive routes (they run retrieval-heavy queries).

I can draft the amendment if you want me to gate the legal language and SOW. Also recommend we offer a limited audit window clause so they feel safe on usage.

M
Monica Patel
Sr. Sales Director | Redwood Inference
(monique signature lines omitted)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Pierce <jpierce@orchid.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, procurement@orchid.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal v3 attached — $750k midpoint, Q3 front-load option, sprint credits defined

Jordan / Procurement team —

Attached is Proposal v3 and a short Amendment + SOW. Highlights:
- Mapped the "standard ramp" to a $750k annual commitment (aligned to your $650k-$900k band).
- Q3 front-load: option to allocate up to +20% of committed monthly capacity for up to two consecutive months; if used, the additional capacity will be billed at the overage rate with a 10% discount applied to that overage portion.
- Sprint credits: 150M token pool, convertible at 1:1, expiration 90 days after contract effective date.
- Overages: capped at a negotiated ceiling (we propose 3x the committed per-token rate) with built-in monthly notifications at 80%/95% thresholds.
- SLA: latency credit tier for their identified routes; language in the amendment.

Please review and tell me if procurement needs any specific redlines — happy to push a tracked-amendment.

Attachment: Orchid_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf (PDF, 3 pages); Amendment-SOW.docx (Word, 2 pages)

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(dylan_brooks@redwood.com)

From: Jordan Pierce <jpierce@orchid.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, procurement@orchid.ai
Date: 2026-11-04T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal v3 attached — $750k midpoint, Q3 front-load option, sprint credits defined

Dylan / Monica —

Thanks — this is close. Procurement asked a couple of small redlines:
1) Reduce the sprint credit pool to 125M tokens if we can get the Q3 front-load priced at 7% below the standard overage rate (we want both concessions).
2) Change the overage ceiling from 3x to 2.5x if SLA credits apply for two consecutive months.
3) Insert a 30-day transparent usage audit clause (they want to confirm consumption patterns once in the first 6 months).

If Redwood can accept 1–3, procurement will circulate a countersigned amendment and we can lock the renewal. I copied procurement on the thread; Mark, if you want to add legal language I can route back.

Jordan
Head of Engineering | Orchid Labs
